serverInfo.name: lean-ctx
serverInfo.title: LeanCTX
serverInfo.description: Context Gateway for AI agents: task-relevant context, supported controls, local knowledge and observable evidence.

result.instructions:
lean-ctx routing — the host's built-in tools map to:
• Read/cat -> ctx_read(path, mode)
• Grep -> ctx_search(pattern, path)
• Shell/bash -> ctx_shell(command)
• Glob/find -> ctx_glob(pattern)
• ls/find -> ctx_tree(path, depth)
This covers built-in file/search/shell tools only; other MCP servers keep their own jobs.

By task:
• Unfamiliar code -> ctx_compose (search + read + symbols in one call)
• Read -> ctx_read(mode=signatures|map|full); edit -> ctx_patch
• Symbol -> ctx_search(action=symbol); meaning -> ctx_search(action=semantic)
• Callers/impact -> ctx_callgraph; memory -> ctx_session

RECOVER: compression is reversible — read the shown path (no MCP) or ctx_read(raw=true), never re-read line-by-line.

ROOTS: ctx_* read ~ projects, write the active one; ~/.ssh etc. closed. Use native Read for out-of-root; `lean-ctx doctor` shows effective roots.

Other tools: ctx_call(tool=<name>).
OUTPUT STYLE: concise
- Bullet points over paragraphs
- Skip filler words and hedging ("I think", "probably", "it seems")
- 1-sentence explanations max, then code/action
- No repeating what the user said


Full instructions at ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md




lean-ctx 3.12.6 (official, https://github.com/yvgude/lean-ctx)

tools.name: ctx_call
tools.description:
Invoke any non-core lean-ctx tool by name — for tools not exposed as standalone MCP tools.
Categories: arch, debug, memory, batch, agent, util. Find exact names with
ctx_discover_tools (query=keyword; empty query lists all). Cannot invoke itself.

tools.name: ctx_callgraph
tools.description:
Callers/callees for one symbol (function call edges, not const/var refs).
action=callers|callees symbol='fn' → every call site with file:line.
action=trace from→to finds the path between two symbols (depth=N).
For end-to-end flow understanding use ctx_compose FIRST.

tools.name: ctx_compose
tools.description: First-pass context for one task; returns ranked files and inline source — use instead of search→read chains.

task.description: Short English task/question or symbol names

task_aware.description: Rank compose sections against the task (default: true)

tools.name: ctx_expand
tools.description:
Retrieve archived tool output: see [Archived:ID] → ctx_expand id=ID (zero-loss, original preserved). head/tail/search filter lines; action=list|search_all browses/queries archives.
ANTIPATTERN: not for project files — use ctx_read or ctx_compose.

id.description: Archive ID, shell_* job ID, or @F1 ref

tools.name: ctx_glob
tools.description:
Find files by glob pattern (respects .gitignore; multi-root via paths).
For file CONTENT search use ctx_search.

tools.name: ctx_patch
tools.description: Safe file edit, project-relative paths. replace_unique(path,old_text,new_text): exact unique replacement, needs no anchors. Line ops take line+hash from ctx_read(mode="anchored:N-M"); CONFLICT means re-read. ops[] batch (cross-file, incl. replace_unique/replace_symbol); create and replace_all only as top-level calls. A 0-byte file: create, or replace_unique with old_text="".

tools.name: ctx_read
tools.description:
Read files. No mode: ≤300 lines whole, larger files as outline with line ranges.
symbol=Name or lines:N-M reads just that part, also for edits.
To UNDERSTAND code run ctx_compose FIRST.

engine_interface.description: Opt into one receipt-backed Engine v1 invocation (single-path aggressive reads only)

mode.description: Default auto. full=complete(edit-ready; ≤turn budget, raw=true beyond) anchored=+N:hh|anchors(line ops) raw=exact-bytes signatures=API map=structure auto=smart diff=cache-delta lines:N-M=window -N=tail 5,10-20=multi reference=pointer task=focus

symbol.description: Name or Class.method: only its lines

tools.name: ctx_search
tools.description: Search code: regex(pattern, default) | semantic(query) | symbol(name|handle) | find_related(file_path,line). Read-only. anchored=true enables ctx_patch refs; queries batches regex searches. Run ctx_compose FIRST.

tools.name: ctx_session

keep_recent_turns.description: compact: trailing user turns kept verbatim (default 6)

tools.name: ctx_shell
tools.description:
WORKFLOW: preferred — auto-compresses output (build/test/log).
Big logs: narrow the command (grep, sed -n, head/tail).
[exit:N] on errors (lossless).
POLICY: allowlisted read-only path.
A [BLOCKED] command is permanent; ctx_execute shares the same allowlist — fix with `lean-ctx allow <cmd>`.
ANTIPATTERN: multi-line scripts, sh/bash script.sh, $var-as-command → ctx_execute (when exposed).

background_action.description: Inspect or cancel a background ctx_shell job; terminal status may include archiveId. Evicted/expired jobs return a structured lookup error.

inline.description: Verbatim up to archive.inline_max_bytes, else archived

raw.description: Exact bytes; only for diffs to apply, hashes, encoded output

run_in_background.description: Detach immediately and return a job id. The command keeps timeout_ms (default here: the 1 h ceiling); poll or cancel with background_action and job_id.

timeout_ms.description: Job lifetime in ms (max 3600000) — NOT the inline wait. A command still running at the ~110s foreground cap detaches to a pollable shell_* job and keeps running up to timeout_ms. Overridden by LEAN_CTX_SHELL_TIMEOUT_MS.

tools.name: ctx_tree
tools.description:
Directory tree with file counts per directory. depth=N (default 3);
show_hidden for dotfiles; paths for multi-root.
respect_gitignore filters ignored files (default true).
WORKFLOW: lightweight orientation before ctx_compose.

tools.name: shell
tools.description:
Shell command with auto-compression (~95 patterns). Alias for ctx_shell.
Output is compressed for token savings. Big logs: narrow the command (grep, sed -n, head/tail).
Use when your MCP client prefers shell/bash over ctx_shell — transparently
delegates to ctx_shell internals.

raw.description: Exact bytes, uncompressed; only for diffs to apply, hashes, encoded output. Default false.

Usage: lean-ctx onboard [--agents <list>] [--dry-run] [--no-agent-aliases]
Connect your AI tools with one command: detects installed
agents, installs hooks/rules/MCP registrations, verifies.
On a terminal it first asks which detected tools to connect.

  --agents <list>     Connect only these tools (e.g. claude,cursor; or none)
                      and remember the choice for updates; `all` connects
                      (and remembers) every tool installed now
  --dry-run           Show what would be written; change nothing
  --yes, -y           Do not ask; connect every detected tool (or the
                      recorded choice)
  --non-interactive   Do not ask; act as without a terminal
  --no-agent-aliases  Do not install claude/codex/gemini shell aliases

Without a terminal and without a recorded choice (npm install, CI) onboard
configures no new tool: it refreshes only tools that already use lean-ctx.
Environment: LEAN_CTX_AGENTS=claude,cursor (or all) works like --agents.
Fine-grained control: lean-ctx setup --help
